frequency_question: How often do federal education authorities successfully execute a formal revocation of a major accrediting body's authority within a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative review process initiated by the U.S. Department of Education targeting the recognized status of a national programmatic or institutional accreditor resulting in a final determination. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probation settlements that do not threaten core recognition.

cases.name: American Bar Association vs. Department of Education (1995-1996 review)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) first termination
ACICS second termination and final de-recognition

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x)
coverage_note: 4 major contested administrative challenges identified; 2 resulted in full revocation, 2 were resolved short of termination.
known_gaps: Lower-level advisory committee recommendations that did not result in final secretarial revocation orders.
skeleton: Total formal de-recognition actions against major federally recognized accreditors over a multi-decade period of heightened regulatory scrutiny.
multiplier: 2 hits out of approximately 4 major contested administrative challenges to national accreditors since 1990.
validity_reason: The regulatory framework governing federal recognition of accreditors remains stable across standard administrative cycles, though shifting political priorities can influence enforcement appetite.
